# Importing Files {.unnumbered}

You can download the zip file referenced in this lesson here: <https://learndata.net/binge.zip>

::: {.content-visible when-profile="stata"}
{{< video https://youtu.be/alrUd8coFro >}}

## Key concepts/commands:

1.  `cd`: set the "working directory," which is the default folder on your computer in which Stata will look for files and output files

    ```         
    cd "C:\Users\favero\OneDrive - american.edu\minus the math\companion guides\datasets\02\example files"
    ```

2.  `import excel`: read in an Excel document as a dataset

    ```         
    import excel using binge.xls, firstrow
    ```

3.  `help`: used to access Stata help files, often for a specific command

    ```         
    help import excel
    ```

4.  `insheet`: old command to read in a plain text file

    ```         
    insheet using binge.tab
    ```

5.  `import delimited`: a newer way to read in a delimited plain text file

    ```         
    import delimited binge.csv
    ```
:::

::: {.content-visible when-profile="r"}
## Model script

``` r
# Note: you'll first need to download binge.zip,
# available at https://learndata.net/binge.zip
# Then, edit the following line to match the folder
# where this file is located.
setwd("C:/Users/favero/Downloads")

#install.packages("rio")  # uncomment if rio not installed
library(rio)

unzip("binge.zip")

data_from_xls <- import("binge.xls")

data_from_dta <- import("binge.dta")

data_from_tab <- import("binge.tab", format = "tsv")
?import

# save the dataset "data_from_tab" as an R object file in my working directory
saveRDS(data_from_tab, file = "binge.rds")
```

## Key concepts/syntax:

1.  `setwd()`: set the "working directory," which is the default folder on your computer in which Stata will look for files and output files

    ``` r
    setwd("C:/Users/favero/learn data/example files")
    ```

2.  `unzip()`: unzip (extract) a zip file

    ``` r
    unzip("binge.zip")
    ```

3.  `?`: open a help file for a function or package

    ``` r
    ?read.delim
    ```

4.  `saveRDS`: save a dataset

    ``` r
    saveRDS(data_from_tab, file = "binge.rds")
    ```
:::
